messages.subject: CFA-singular matrix
parts:
Hello everyone!

I try to run the CFA analysis on a database but I get as an error message that my "matrix is singular".
For exemple, if I want to inverse my matrix, I can't : 

> solve(cov.matrix)
Erreur dans solve.default(cov.matrix) : 
  le système est numériquement singulier : conditionnement de la réciproque = 8.36219e-22

I ran a bivariate analysis to see if I could have a multicolinearity problem with my matrix and I definitely have lot
off variables who are highly correlated (r>0.7).
That's my code :

#Confirmatory factor analysis

##Set working directory

rm(list = ls()) ## Clears R Console
setwd("/home/celine/Documents/Stage NZ/Analysis-R/CFA/CFA Jenny")

##Read in the data
xdata=read.table("standardizedvalues_PCA.csv", header= TRUE)
head(xdata)
summary(xdata)

# latent variable definitions
require(lavaan)
model <- '
Family =~ e019 + a001 + a029 + a030 + a032 + a034 + a035 + a038 + a039 + a041 + a042 + f121
Politics =~  a004 + e023 + e069_05 + e069_11 + e069_12 + e069_13 + e069_14 + + e069_04 + e069_06 + e069_08 + + e069_10 + e069_20 + e037 + e114 + e115 + e116 + e117
Ingroup.outgroup =~ g006 + a124_02 + a124_06 + a124_07
Autonomy.Conformity =~ a002 + a173 + d054 + d055 + e018 + e035
Gender.roles =~ d059 + d060 + e069_15
Religion =~ a040 + f063 + e069_01 + f028 + a006
Morality =~ a165 + f114 + f115 + f116 + f117 + f118 + f119 + f120 + f122 + f123 + e016 + a124_03 + a124_08
Wellbeing.Work =~ c006 + e015 + f001 + a003 + a005 + a008 + a009 + a170

Family ~~ Politics
Family ~~ Ingroup.outgroup
Family ~~ Autonomy.Conformity
Family ~~ Gender.roles
Family ~~ Religion
Family ~~ Morality
Family ~~ Wellbeing.Work
Politics ~~ Ingroup.outgroup

Politics ~~ Gender.roles

Politics ~~ Wellbeing.Work
Ingroup.outgroup ~~ Autonomy.Conformity

Ingroup.outgroup ~~ Morality
Ingroup.outgroup ~~ Wellbeing.Work

Autonomy.Conformity ~~ Wellbeing.Work
Gender.roles ~~ Religion
Gender.roles ~~ Morality
Gender.roles ~~ Wellbeing.Work
Religion ~~ Morality
Religion ~~ Wellbeing.Work
Morality ~~ Wellbeing.Work
'
fit <- cfa(model, data=xdata)

And finally, when I run the cfa model I had this warning message :

Messages d'avis :
1: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, group.label = group.label,  :
  lavaan WARNING: small number of observations (nobs < nvar)
  nobs = 41 nvar = 68
2: In lav_samplestats_from_data(lavdata = lavdata, missing = lavoptions$missing,  :
  lavaan WARNING: sample covariance can not be inverted
3: In lavaan::lavaan(model = model, data = xdata, model.type = "cfa",  :
  lavaan WARNING: model has NOT converged!

I really don't know how I can get around this problem. What is the solution to give a matrix singular--> non-singular?
I'm not very easy with R. But I really want to learn to manage this kind
of problem.If you have time to explain your point of you on this problem,
I would appreciate.
I remain available for more information.

Thanks in advance.

Céline

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: CFA-singular matrix
parts:
Céline--
I think the core of your problem is described in this warning:
lavaan WARNING: small number of observations (nobs < nvar)

When there are more observed variables than cases or respondents, a covariance matrix is going to be unstable.  Perhaps, with a larger sample, the covariance matrix would not have this problem, so one solution would be to get more data.
--Ed Rigdon
